title: Assessment of Hearing Health in Healthcare Workers: Impact of Noise Exposure in Hospital Departments Hearing Health and Noise Exposure in Hospital Staff
official: Assessment of Hearing Health in Healthcare Workers: Impact of Noise Exposure in Hospital Departments Hearing Health and Noise Exposure in Hospital Staff
summary: The SAS project aims to evaluate the impact of chronic noise exposure on the hearing health of 290 hospital healthcare workers. It focuses on detecting "hidden hearing loss" (cochlear synaptopathy) and functional deficits using specific speech-in-noise tests (Odizi digital solution) and questionnaires. A sub-group of symptomatic subjects will undergo advanced electrophysiological and cognitive assessments to identify specific biomarkers of noise-induced auditory neuropathy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthcare worker or staff at CHU Toulouse in targeted departments.
* Age ≥ 18 years
* Affiliated to a social security scheme.
* Signed informed consent.
* Normal hearing (PTA ≤ 25 dB HL in each ear, at frequencies 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 Hz)
* Sufficient command of French to answer the questionnaires.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known moderate to severe hearing loss or use of hearing aids.
* Active outer or middle ear pathology (e.g., earwax blockage, otitis).
* Major neurological or psychiatric disorders interfering with cognitive tests.
* Inability to perform Virtual Reality tests (e.g., severe balance disorders).
* Persons under legal protection/guardianship.
